sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a podcast produced by the American Psychological
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《心理学话题》，这是一个由美国心理学

sentences.en: Association.
sentences.zh: 学会制作的播客。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Audrey Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。

sentences.en: In this episode, I talk with a psychologist about bringing feminism to young girls and teens who are coming of age in a challenging time.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我将与一位心理学家探讨如何将女权主义带给那些在充满挑战的时代中步入青春期的年轻女孩和青少年。

sentences.en: So there's all these things that, you know, show that, hey, we're equal, and we've succeeded, and we've arrived.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些事情，你知道的，都在表明，嘿，我们是平等的，我们已经成功了，我们已经成功抵达了。

sentences.en: And yet, obviously, we can look around our culture and see that we still have a long way to go.
sentences.zh: 然而，显而易见的是，环顾我们的文化，我们可以发现我们仍然有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: More than previous generations, today's teens are being brought up to believe girls can do anything, but they still face the challenges of being a
sentences.zh: 与前几代人相比，如今的青少年从小就被灌输女孩无所不能的观念，但她们仍然面临着作为

sentences.en: teenage girl, and that does include increased rates of depression and low self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 青春期女孩的挑战，这确实包括抑郁症和低自尊发病率的上升。

sentences.en: But according to our guest, feminist psychological theory and practice could be used to better
sentences.zh: 但根据我们嘉宾的说法，女权主义心理学理论和实践可以用来更好地

sentences.en: support teenage girls while giving them the courage to face the challenges of adolescence.
sentences.zh: 支持青春期女孩，同时赋予她们面对青春期挑战的勇气。

sentences.en: Gail Pittman is a psychology and women's gender studies professor at Sacramento City College.
sentences.zh: 盖尔·皮特曼是萨克拉门托城市学院的一名心理学和妇女性别研究教授。

sentences.en: She's also a children's book author and has written several books published by Imagination
sentences.zh: 她还是一位儿童读物作家，由幻想

sentences.en: Press, focusing on LGBTQ issues for children.
sentences.zh: 出版社出版了多部专注于儿童 LGBTQ 议题的书籍。

sentences.en: Her latest book is called Feminism A to Z.
sentences.zh: 她的最新力作名为《从 A 到 Z 认识女权主义》。

sentences.en: It's a hands-on introduction for teens and tweens who are interested in learning about feminism.
sentences.zh: 这是一本为对了解女权主义感兴趣的青少年和准青少年准备的实用入门书。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Pittman.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，皮特曼博士。

sentences.en: Hi, thank you.
sentences.zh: 嗨，谢谢你。

sentences.en: So your latest book, Feminism A to Z.
sentences.zh: 那么你的新书《从 A 到 Z 认识女权主义》。

sentences.en: I'm interested to hear what this book is about and who it's for.
sentences.zh: 我很想听听这本书是关于什么的，以及它是写给谁看的。

sentences.en: It is exactly what it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 它就像听起来的那样。

sentences.en: It's feminism from A to Z.
sentences.zh: 这就是从 A 到 Z 的女权主义。

sentences.en: It's intended as a book for teenagers and potentially older tweens kind of in that ballpark, depending on how mature the child is.
sentences.zh: 它旨在成为一本适合青少年以及可能在这个年龄段稍大一点的准青少年的书，具体取决于孩子的成熟度。

sentences.en: Basically giving kids an introduction to the world of feminism.
sentences.zh: 基本上是为孩子们提供进入女权主义世界的入门指南。

sentences.en: And I structured it as an A to Z by chapter.
sentences.zh: 我按章节将其结构化为从 A 到 Z 的顺序。

sentences.en: So each chapter has a focus that's organized by letters.
sentences.zh: 因此，每一章都有一个按字母组织的核心焦点。

sentences.en: So like, for example, the first chapter is called A is for Anger.
sentences.zh: 比如，举个例子，第一章叫“A 代表愤怒”。

sentences.en: And it outlines the reasons why girls and women might be angry about the various injustices that have been committed against them over the centuries, really.
sentences.zh: 它概述了为什么女孩和女性可能会对几个世纪以来针对她们的各种不公义行为感到愤怒的原因，真的。

sentences.en: As well as how women and girls who are angry are perceived, right?
sentences.zh: 以及感到愤怒的女性和女孩是如何被看待的，对吧？

sentences.en: Like anger and femininity tend not to go together, at least in our culture.
sentences.zh: 就像愤怒和女性气质往往格格不入一样，至少在我们的文化中是这样。

sentences.en: So that's the focus for that chapter.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那一章的重点。

sentences.en: And then each chapter also has a history focus, focusing on some element of women's history or feminist history or what have you.
sentences.zh: 然后每一章还有一个历史焦点，聚焦于女性历史、女权主义历史或其他相关内容的某些方面。

sentences.en: And then there's an activity called
sentences.zh: 接着还有一个名为

sentences.en: Try This.
sentences.zh: “试一试”的活动。

sentences.en: So it really gets kids into action, kind of out of their heads and into their hands and heart, if you will, and finding ways to take action in their own lives.
sentences.zh: 因此，它真正让孩子们参与到行动中，摆脱纯粹的空想，用双手和心灵去实践，如果你愿意的话，在他们自己的生活中寻找采取行动的方法。

sentences.en: So it's really intended for a teenage audience, although you could scale it up or scale it back depending on the maturity of the child.
sentences.zh: 所以它真正面向的是青少年读者，尽管你可以根据孩子的成熟度向上或向下调整。

sentences.en: It's, I was just going to say, I imagine this is difficult because for teenagers and the kids that age, they're very much in their own heads and their own worlds, right?
sentences.zh: 我正想说，我想这很不容易，因为对于青少年和那个年龄的孩子来说，他们非常沉浸在自己的内心世界里，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, that is what is most important to them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这才是对他们最重要的事。

sentences.en: So I'm curious, you know, why you thought that it's important to bring the message of feminism to a group like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，你知道的，为什么你认为向这样一个群体传递女权主义的信息是很重要的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, I teach women and gender studies at Sacramento City College.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在萨克拉门托城市学院教妇女和性别研究。

sentences.en: And so, you know, a lot of my students are 18, 19, 20 years old, sometimes older than that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我的很多学生都是 18、19、20 岁，有时比这还要大。

sentences.en: And I think that that's usually the age where girls and women start to learn about feminism, start to become more aware.
sentences.zh: 我认为这通常是女孩和女性开始了解女权主义、开始提高意识的年龄。

sentences.en: And, and yet, I think that if girls were introduced to some of the concepts of feminism earlier, that that could really help them weather the storms of adolescence.
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为如果能让女孩们更早接触到女权主义的一些概念，那将真正有助于她们度过青春期的风风雨雨。

sentences.en: Because I think that not only are there the physical and cognitive changes that happen during adolescence, there's also kind of
sentences.zh: 因为我认为青春期不仅有身体和认知上的变化，还有一种

sentences.en: a level of awareness that teens start to get, an awareness that the world may not be what they thought it was when they were children.
sentences.zh: 青少年开始获得的意识，一种意识到世界可能并不像他们小时候想象的那样的意识。

sentences.en: They become more aware of sexism and racism and homophobia and transphobia and other types of injustices.
sentences.zh: 他们开始更加意识到性别歧视、种族主义、恐同症、跨性别恐惧症和其他类型的不公义。

sentences.en: And yet they may not necessarily, they have the, they have the cognitive tools to understand it intellectually, but they may not necessarily have the emotional tools
sentences.zh: 然而他们未必一定拥有——他们拥有在智力上理解它的认知工具，但他们未必一定具备情感上的工具

sentences.en: or the maturity to be able to navigate those kinds of realities.
sentences.zh: 或成熟度来应对这些现实。

sentences.en: And I think that feminism can offer a set of tools, if you will, to help them wrap their heads around this in their own lives.
sentences.zh: 我认为女权主义可以提供一套工具，如果你愿意的话，来帮助他们在自己的生活中理清头绪。

sentences.en: So that's really why I decided to write the book.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的是我决定写这本书的原因。

sentences.en: Is there research out there to show that young girls, teenagers are more likely to identify as feminists than older generations?
sentences.zh: 有没有研究表明，年轻女孩和青少年比老一代人更有可能认同自己是女权主义者？

sentences.en: And, you know, do their ideas of feminism line up with older generations ideas?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，她们对女权主义的看法是否与老一代人的看法一致？

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So there's really two questions there, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这里实际上有两个问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Are millennials likely to call themselves feminists and why or why not, depending.
sentences.zh: 千禧一代是否倾向于自称女权主义者，为什么或者为什么不，视情况而定。

sentences.en: And if they do, do their ideas of feminism line up with other generations?
sentences.zh: 如果她们是，她们对女权主义的看法是否与其他代人一致？

sentences.en: And so what I've seen in the research, and I haven't seen anything like super recently, but what I've seen over the years is that generally the further away we get
sentences.zh: 所以我在研究中看到的是——我没看过特别近期的研究，但我多年来看到的是，通常我们离

sentences.en: from like the 1960s, 1970s era of feminism, the less likely we tend to see girls and women identifying as feminists.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪 60 年代、70 年代的女权主义时代越远，女孩和女性认同为女权主义者的可能性就越小。

sentences.en: There was a bit of a blip during the 90s, which a lot of people refer to as the quote-unquote third wave of feminism, although there's lots of people that don't like wave models
sentences.zh: 90 年代曾有过一个小插曲，许多人称之为所谓的女权主义“第三次浪潮”，尽管有很多人并不一定喜欢浪潮模型

sentences.en: necessarily, and there's some discussion of that in the book.
sentences.zh: ，书中对此也有一些探讨。

sentences.en: I think that especially for millennials,
sentences.zh: 我认为，特别是对千禧一代来说，

sentences.en: they're a generation that's kind of caught between a rock and a hard place.
sentences.zh: 他们是夹在夹心饼干里的一代人。

sentences.en: And what I mean by that is that they're growing up in an era where they have more rights than ever before, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们在一个拥有比以往任何时候都多的权利的时代长大，对吧？

sentences.en: Like they
sentences.zh: 就像他们

sentences.en: have the right to go to school, they have the right to learn how to read, they have the right to
sentences.zh: 有上学的权利，有学习阅读的权利，有

sentences.en: open up their own checking account.
sentences.zh: 开立自己支票账户的权利。

sentences.en: I mean, things that we just take for granted, which a couple of generations ago was not necessarily the case.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些我们视为理所当然的事情，在几代人之前却并非如此。

sentences.en: And so there's all these things that, you know, show that, hey, we're equal and we've succeeded and we've arrived.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些事情，你知道的，都在表明，嘿，我们是平等的，我们成功了，我们抵达了。

sentences.en: And yet, obviously, we can look around our culture and see that we still have a long way to go.
sentences.zh: 然而，显而易见的是，环顾我们的文化，我们可以发现我们仍然有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: And so because of that, I don't think that most teens and young adults today identify with like the old school kind of feminism of the 70s.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我认为当今的大多数青少年和年轻人并不认同 70 年代那种老派的女权主义。

sentences.en: And I think that's what a lot of people think of when they think of feminism.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是很多人一想到女权主义时脑海中浮现的画面。

sentences.en: You know, they think of like holding banners and marching and, I don't know, burning their bras, which interestingly is a myth that never happened.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们会想到举着标语游行，以及，我不知道，烧掉胸罩，有趣的是，这从未发生过。

sentences.en: But, you know, seriously.
sentences.zh: 但是，说真的。

sentences.en: Is it really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It was basically a form of propaganda that was, you know, flooded throughout the media to try to convince people not to be
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一种宣传手段，你知道的，充斥在各大媒体中，试图说服人们不要成为

sentences.en: feminiSt. And it worked because you still hear that phrase today.
sentences.zh: 女权主义者。而且它奏效了，因为你今天仍然能听到这种说法。

sentences.en: So I think that's what a lot of
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是许多

sentences.en: girls and young women think of when they think of feminism.
sentences.zh: 女孩和年轻女性在想到女权主义时所想到的。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I do with my students on the first day of class, in my Psych of Women class, is ask them to write down what words come to mind.
sentences.zh: 我在女性心理学课上第一天对学生做的事情之一，就是让他们写下脑海中浮现的词汇。

sentences.en: We do sort of like a free association activity.
sentences.zh: 我们做了一种自由联想的活动。

sentences.en: What words come to mind when they hear the word feminist?
sentences.zh: 当他们听到“女权主义者”这个词时，脑海里会浮现出什么词？

sentences.en: And it's so fascinating because there's all these words that come up, some of which are empowering, some of which are really negative.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了，因为会涌现出各种各样的词，其中一些令人鼓舞，另一些则非常负面。

sentences.en: And then we start to unpack the actual definitions of feminism and some of the different feminist philosophies.
sentences.zh: 然后我们开始剖析女权主义的实际定义以及一些不同的女权主义哲学。

sentences.en: And that's one of the things that the early chapters of feminism from A to Z does is start to shine a light on the fact that there
sentences.zh: 这就是《从 A 到 Z 认识女权主义》早期章节所做的事情之一，开始阐明这样一个事实：

sentences.en: isn't just one way to be feminiSt. There's a variety of different approaches to it, a variety of
sentences.zh: 成为女权主义者并非只有一种方式。它有各种不同的方法，有各种

sentences.en: different theoretical perspectives, depending on who you are, depending on your social location, depending on a variety of different things.
sentences.zh: 不同的理论视角，这取决于你是谁、你的社会阶层以及各种不同的因素。

sentences.en: And once students start to recognize that, then they're much more likely to buy into it.
sentences.zh: 一旦学生们开始认识到这一点，他们就更有可能接受它。

sentences.en: But I think it's the label.
sentences.zh: 但我认为问题出在标签上。

sentences.en: Like there's something about the word that kind of makes girls and, you know, makes millennials in particular say, oh, no, that's not me.
sentences.zh: 就像这个词本身有些东西，让女孩们，你知道的，尤其是让千禧年代的人说，哦，不，那不是我。

sentences.en: That's, you know, that's something different.
sentences.zh: 那是，你知道的，那是完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: So in this age of social media, girls are also getting, I would say, very mixed messages about what's okay to share, what's the right way to do things.
sentences.zh: 所以在社交媒体时代，女孩们也收到了，我想说，关于什么可以分享、什么是做事正确方式的非常混杂的信息。

sentences.en: But it's also easy for them to connect with each other, you know, find other people who share their views.
sentences.zh: 但对她们来说，彼此联系、你知道的、找到与自己观点相同的人也很容易。

sentences.en: How do you think social media is shaping the feminist movement now among younger generations and is, or is it hindering the movement?
sentences.zh: 你认为社交媒体现在是如何塑造年轻一代的女权主义运动的？它是在阻碍这场运动吗？

sentences.en: You know, I hear a lot of people say that millennials are not very politically active, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我听到很多人说千禧一代不是很积极参与政治，对吧？

sentences.en: Like they don't care about politics, they don't stay on top of social issues, etc.
sentences.zh: 就像他们不关心政治，不关注社会议题等等。

sentences.en: And I, I don't know, maybe I live in a bubble with my students, but I would disagree.
sentences.zh: 而我，我不知道，也许我和我的学生生活在一个泡沫里，但我不敢苟同。

sentences.en: I would say that they pay attention differently than previous generations did, and that a lot of their activism stems from social media.
sentences.zh: 我会说他们的关注方式与前几代人不同，他们的许多行动主义都源于社交媒体。

sentences.en: I mean, I think, for example, about the Black Lives Matter movement, which isn't necessarily a feminist movement, although
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比如我想到了“黑人的命也是命”运动，这不一定是一个女权主义运动，尽管

sentences.en: there's a feminist intersection there, that started as a Twitter hashtag.
sentences.zh: 其中存在女权主义的交集，它是作为推特标签开始的。

sentences.en: I mean, that was an act of, you know, I mean, that was a form of social media activism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是，你知道的，那是一种社交媒体行动主义的形式。

sentences.en: We think a number of years ago about the
sentences.zh: 我们回想几年前的

sentences.en: Occupy movement.
sentences.zh: “占领”运动。

sentences.en: That also started on social media.
sentences.zh: 这也是在社交媒体上开始的。

sentences.en: The March on Washington after the election, where, you know, women across the country were knitting, you know, pink hats, you know, pink pussy hats.
sentences.zh: 选举后的华盛顿大游行，你知道的，全国各地的女性都在织粉色帽子，你知道的，粉色猫耳帽。

sentences.en: That started as a social media trend.
sentences.zh: 那是作为一个社交媒体趋势开始的。

sentences.en: And so I think there's a lot of opportunity for activism and connecting that way using various social media platforMs. The downside that I see is that there's
sentences.zh: 所以我认为利用各种社交媒体平台，有很大的机会进行行动主义和建立联系。我看到的缺点是，

sentences.en: something very powerful about, like, people physically getting together and having a conversation in real time that's not hindered by technology.
sentences.zh: 人们聚在一起，进行不受技术阻碍的实时对话，有一种非常强大的力量。

sentences.en: And I, I don't know, I think it's a little early to tell whether or not it's social media and technology in general is a hindrance to that.
sentences.zh: 而且我，我不知道，我认为现在判断社交媒体和整体技术是否对此构成阻碍还为时过早。

sentences.en: I just see a lot less, you know, like, personal engagement in that way.
sentences.zh: 我只是看到那种面对面的、个人参与明显减少了。

sentences.en: There's a lot of online engagement and technology-infused engagement.
sentences.zh: 有很多线上参与和融入技术的参与。

sentences.en: But in terms of face-to-face, like, boots-on-the-ground type of organizing, and even just brainstorming and, you know, just sharing, you know, sharing some
sentences.zh: 但在面对面、基层组织方面，甚至只是头脑风暴，你知道的，仅仅分享，分享

sentences.en: everyone's narratives and life stories.
sentences.zh: 每个人的叙事和生活故事。

sentences.en: I think that that's, it remains to be seen, I think, how social media impacts that process.
sentences.zh: 我认为这，社交媒体如何影响这一过程还有待观察。

sentences.en: Your work also focuses on educating students on LGBTQ history.
sentences.zh: 你的工作也专注于向学生普及 LGBTQ 历史。

sentences.en: You know, one of your other Imagination Press books, When You Look Out the Window.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你的另一本幻想出版社的书，《当你望向窗外》。你能稍微谈谈那本书是关于什么的吗？

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit about that book, what it's about?
sentences.zh: 你能稍微谈谈那本书，它是关于什么的？

sentences.en: And why do you think it's important for parents and educators to teach children these stories?
sentences.zh: 为什么你认为父母和教育工作者向孩子传授这些故事很重要？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So When You Look Out the Window is a picture book biography about lesbian activist couple, Phyllis Lyon and Del Martin, who, if you live in the San
sentences.zh: 所以《当你望向窗外》是一本关于女同性恋活动家伴侣菲利斯·里昂和德尔·马丁的图画书传记，如果你住在旧金

sentences.en: Francisco Bay Area, like, almost everybody knows who they are, because they are just iconic.
sentences.zh: 山湾区，几乎每个人都知道他们是谁，因为他们简直是标志性人物。

sentences.en: But if you live outside of that area, lots, you know, there's people within the LGBT community who may know who
sentences.zh: 但如果你住在该地区之外，很多人，你知道的，LGBT 社区内可能有人知道

sentences.en: they are and what their contributions are, but I would say that the vast majority of people are just completely unfamiliar with their activism.
sentences.zh: 他们是谁以及他们的贡献是什么，但我可以说绝大多数人对他们的行动主义完全不了解。

sentences.en: And the reality is, is that they, I think, in many ways, launched the LGBT movement back in the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，我认为他们在很多方面在 20 世纪 50 年代就发起了 LGBTQ 运动。

sentences.en: And when we think about Stonewall, the Stonewall riots is kind of the beginning of the modern day LGBT social justice movement.
sentences.zh: 当我们想到石墙时，石墙暴动被认为是现代 LGBTQ 社会正义运动的开端。

sentences.en: But if you go back a couple of decades earlier, back to the 1950s, when Phyllis and Del met and then moved in together and, you know,
sentences.zh: 但如果你把时间往前推几十年，回到 20 世纪 50 年代，当菲利斯和德尔相遇并同居，然后，你知道的，

sentences.en: started their activist journey, the landscape was very harsh.
sentences.zh: 开始她们的活动家之旅时，当时的社会环境非常严酷。

sentences.en: I mean, it was the post-war era, it was the era of McCarthyism and the Red Scare and fear of anyone who was potentially communist or different
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是战后时期，是麦卡锡主义和红色恐怖的时代，人们害怕任何可能是共产主义者、异类

sentences.en: or leftist or not mainstream in any way, whatever way.
sentences.zh: 、左翼分子或任何不主流的人。

sentences.en: And that was the environment that Phyllis and
sentences.zh: 这就是菲利斯和

sentences.en: Del were living in in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 德尔在旧金山生活的环境。

sentences.en: And instead of hiding or instead of, you know, kind of staying under the radar, they were out and loud and proud and, you know, just like pounded the pavement until
sentences.zh: 她们没有选择隐藏，也没有选择，你知道的，保持低调，而是公开、大声而自豪地，你知道的，就像踏平了每条街道，直到

sentences.en: Del died in 2008.
sentences.zh: 德尔于 2008 年去世。

sentences.en: And so I think that their story is really powerful.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们的故事真的非常震撼。

sentences.en: And that is one of the reasons that I wanted to write this.
sentences.zh: 这也是我想写这本书的原因之一。

sentences.en: And the other thing, kind of going to your second question, is that I worry a lot that these narratives, if they don't get written down or if they don't get passed down
sentences.zh: 另一件事，顺着你的第二个问题，我很担心这些叙事如果不被写下来，或者如果不以某种形式

sentences.en: in some way, shape or form, that they're going to get loSt. I mean, there's lots of LGBT history
sentences.zh: 代代相传，它们就会失落。我的意思是，有很多 LGBTQ 历史

sentences.en: that's already been lost, largely because LGBT people typically don't live in families with other
sentences.zh: 已经失落了，很大程度上是因为 LGBTQ 人群通常不与其他

sentences.en: LGBT people.
sentences.zh: LGBTQ 人群生活在同一个家庭中。

sentences.en: They're kind of in isolation and have to find community in some way.
sentences.zh: 他们处于某种孤立状态，必须以某种方式寻找社区。

sentences.en: So there isn't that kind of natural passing down of stories, you know, that kind of oral tradition, that oral narrative
sentences.zh: 所以并没有那种故事的自然传承，你知道的，那种口头传统，那种口头叙事

sentences.en: that you see, say, in communities of color or other marginalized groups where people have shared identities.
sentences.zh: 你在有共同身份的有色人种社区或其他边缘化群体中看到的那种传承。

sentences.en: In the LGBT community, that's a much more difficult kind of process.
sentences.zh: 在 LGBTQ 社区，这是一个困难得多的过程。

sentences.en: And so if people aren't writing these down or recording them in some way, it's easy for those stories to get loSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果人们不把这些写下来或以某种方式记录下来，这些故事就很容易失落。

sentences.en: And I'm seeing it already in my classroom.
sentences.zh: 我已经从我的课堂上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, when I teach about sexuality and gender,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我教授性取向和性别时，

sentences.en: lots of my students don't know anything about the Stonewall riots.
sentences.zh: 我的很多学生对石墙暴动一无所知。

sentences.en: They've never heard of
sentences.zh: 他们从未听说过

sentences.en: Phyllis Lyon and Del Martin.
sentences.zh: 菲利斯·里昂和德尔·马丁。

sentences.en: They didn't know about McCarthyism and the Red Scare.
sentences.zh: 他们对麦卡锡主义和红色恐慌一无所知。

sentences.en: Increasingly, and this is really scary to me, considering that this is within my own lifetime.
sentences.zh: 越来越严重的是，而且这让我感到非常害怕，考虑到这竟然发生在我有生之年。

sentences.en: There's lots of students that are unaware about the magnitude of the AIDS crisis and the ways in which the government
sentences.zh: 有许多学生完全不了解艾滋病危机的严重程度，以及政府

sentences.en: did or didn't intervene to try to prevent further deaths from happening.
sentences.zh: 是否进行了干预，或者没有干预，以试图阻止更多死亡的发生。

sentences.en: And so when they learn of this, they become, number one, surprised.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们了解到这一点时，首先，他们会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And then number two, really angry, especially my LGBTQ identified students.
sentences.zh: 其次，他们会非常生气，尤其是我的LGBTQ群体的学生。

sentences.en: I mean, the first question they'll ask is, how come nobody ever taught us this?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们问的第一个问题是，为什么从来没有人教过我们这些？

sentences.en: This is unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 这简直难以置信。

sentences.en: And I think it's a symptom of a larger problem of history is not necessarily getting passed down.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是历史没有被很好地传承下来的更大问题的一个征兆。

sentences.en: And I think a great place to start is with children.
sentences.zh: 我认为一个很好的切入点就是从孩子开始。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: This is kind of just a side question, but I'm curious.
sentences.zh: 这其实只是一个衍生问题，但我很好奇。

sentences.en: You're a psychologiSt. You're a college professor.
sentences.zh: 你是一位心理学家，你是一位大学教授。

sentences.en: Tell me how you got involved in writing children's books.
sentences.zh: 能告诉我你是怎么开始涉足儿童绘本创作的吗？

sentences.en: That's a fair question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很合理的问题。

sentences.en: You know, like what was it about children's books that, and I think you touched a little bit just
sentences.zh: 你知道的，儿童绘本有什么吸引人之处，而且我想你刚才已经稍微提到了一点

sentences.en: now on that, you know, like you said, like passing down these stories to children, you know, or somewhere to start with that, right?
sentences.zh: ，正如你所说，把这些故事传承给孩子们，你知道的，或者从某个地方开始入手，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This is, actually, it's good that you asked that question because my path to writing children's books is a kind of twisty and turny one.
sentences.zh: 其实，你问得很好，因为我走上儿童文学创作的道路可以说是曲折蜿蜒的。

sentences.en: So I have a friend outside of my academic work and psychology and all of that, who's a children's book writer and illustrator.
sentences.zh: 我在学术研究和心理学工作之外有一个朋友，她是一位儿童图书作家兼插画家。

sentences.en: And she was an academic in children's writing and creative writing at a university.
sentences.zh: 她曾在某所大学担任儿童文学和创意写作的学者。

sentences.en: And she, at some point in her career, decided to step back from academia and do her writing and illustrating full time and also launch writing classes.
sentences.zh: 在职业生涯的某个阶段，她决定淡出学术界，全职从事写作和插画工作，并开设了写作班。

sentences.en: So she had just moved to Sacramento.
sentences.zh: 当时她刚搬到萨克拉门托。

sentences.en: She was launching her very first class.
sentences.zh: 她正在筹办自己的第一个班级。

sentences.en: She was trying to drum up business.
sentences.zh: 她当时在极力招揽生意。

sentences.en: I ran into her one day.
sentences.zh: 有一天我偶遇了她。

sentences.en: She was telling me about her class and she basically twisted my arm and I'm not fabulous at saying no.
sentences.zh: 她跟我讲了她的班级，基本上是软磨硬泡地劝说我，而我又很不擅长拒绝别人。

sentences.en: So I said yes.
sentences.zh: 所以我答应了。

sentences.en: And then afterwards I was like, oh my gosh, I can't believe I said yes to this.
sentences.zh: 事后我在想，天哪，我怎么会答应这种事。

sentences.en: I can't do this.
sentences.zh: 我做不来。

sentences.en: I don't have time.
sentences.zh: 我没有时间。

sentences.en: Blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 巴拉巴拉之类的。

sentences.en: But oh my gosh, this class was unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 但是天哪，这个班级简直太棒了。

sentences.en: It was so much fun.
sentences.zh: 太有趣了。

sentences.en: It just opened up a whole different area of my brain, I guess you could say.
sentences.zh: 你可以说它彻底打开了我大脑中一个全然不同的领域。

sentences.en: A whole different form of creativity.
sentences.zh: 一种完全不同的创造力形式。

sentences.en: And it was, once I started doing that type of writing and then getting a sense of the
sentences.zh: 一旦我开始尝试那种写作，然后对儿童图书的市场有了了解

sentences.en: landscape of kids' books and seeing what was there but also what wasn't there, like who wasn't being
sentences.zh: ，看到了现有的作品，同时也看到了缺失的内容，比如谁没有在儿童读物中得到

sentences.en: represented in children's books and what wasn't being written about, that I got even more motivated to start focusing my energy in that direction.
sentences.zh: 代表，以及有什么主题还没有被书写，这让我更有动力把精力集中在这个方向上。

sentences.en: Well, great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Pittman, thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 皮特曼博士，非常感谢您做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: It's been a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 非常荣幸。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听。
